summary:
AEGIS is tracking 11 active global security events across 14 countries and territories. 1 is rated Critical and 7 High; 3 Moderate and 0 Low events are under observation. 0 events were substantively updated in the last 24 hours.

Critical events: Iranian strikes on Bahrain and continuing attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz (Bahrain, Iran).

High-priority events: Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles land in Poland during attacks on Ukraine (Poland, Russia); Russian ballistic missile strike on central Kryvyi Rih kills two, wounds 60 (Ukraine, Russia); Suspected Ukrainian sea-drone strike damages Russian corvette at Benghazi naval base (Libya, Russia); Global cyber campaign against industrial refrigeration and cold-chain systems (Multiple, France).

By region, activity is recorded in Europe (3), Global (3), Africa (2), North America (2), Asia-Pacific (1), Middle East (1), Latin America (1). By primary category: military (6), cybersecurity (2), geopolitical (1), AI (1), environmental (1).

Evidence status across active events: 7 confirmed, 4 reported, 0 disputed and 0 analytical assessments. Trends: 4 escalating, 7 stable and 0 de-escalating.

The Emerging Global Security Signals panel lists 2 observed actions, such as preparedness guidance, exercises, official warnings and new advisories. A signal records what was observed; it does not by itself establish an imminent threat.

Priority reflects impact, evidence quality, exposure, geographic scope, observed activity and urgency, not media attention, and is kept separate from evidence status. Reported allegations remain attributed claims until supported by independent evidence. Volume of reporting about a country is not a measure of its threat level. Each assessment lists its sources, unknowns and full update history.
